name: Religious anti-Zionism
summary: Religious anti-Zionism, in its Jewish Haredi form, holds that a Jewish state established before the Messiah rebels against God and the nations, in breach of the Three Oaths, and delays redemption. Its adherents refuse to vote in, fund themselves from, or recognise the state, while living peaceably under other governments and keeping a strictly traditional communal life. A small fringe, Neturei Karta, goes further and calls for the state's dismantling and Palestinian rule.
scope: The Satmar line of Joel Teitelbaum's Vayoel Moshe and the Edah HaChareidis circle, with Neturei Karta as a radical wing; it excludes Agudat Yisrael-style Haredi non-Zionism that votes and accepts state funds, and Christian and Muslim religious anti-Zionism. Economic, technology and many general-politics statements are inferred and low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nothing in the Satmar sources addresses healthcare; refusal of Israeli state benefits is about non-participation in the Zionist state, while Haredi communities elsewhere use public provision, so adherents are split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The sources do not treat wage law; Haredi communities mix small-business and communal-charity outlooks, so no clear lean can be inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: No source states a view on market efficiency; communal Haredi economies combine private enterprise with charity and mutual aid.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred: a community that refuses state funds and builds its own independent institutions is unlikely to favour state ownership of industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed; Haredi tradition values tzedakah by voluntary giving, but adherents have no stated stance on state taxation of the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not discussed in the sources; Haredi communities generally favour the community's own bodies over secular labour organisations.

property-fundamental.rationale: Halakha protects property, but the sources never frame it as a near-inviolable political right, so the inference is weak.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The sources do not address corporate regulation; no confident lean can be drawn.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: Satmar rejects Israeli state welfare for religious reasons, but many Haredim elsewhere depend on benefits and charity is central, so adherents lean against cutting welfare for the needy.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: a traditional religious community has no program of workers collectively owning firms; economic life runs through family and communal enterprise.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Haredi communities distrust state intrusion but also value security against terrorism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from Teitelbaum's strict moral and ritual discipline and ban on television, which suggests opposition to recreational drug legalisation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not discussed; adherents prize their own religious speech freedom yet have used herem against critics, so no clear lean.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred: authority is vested in rabbinic leaders and the Messiah, while a human strongman bypassing gridlock is not part of the teaching.

state-harmful.rationale: The Satmar view holds that only the Israeli Zionist state is illegitimate; peaceful life under gentile governments is endorsed, so the state in general is not rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no stated stance for either side.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: Haredim refuse IDF service and treat Zionist military power as a violation of the oath not to rebel against the nations.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Teitelbaum's strict sexual-modesty rules (tznius) show strong opposition to legalising prostitution on halakhic grounds.

decide-locally.rationale: Inferred from the Satmar pattern of self-governing independent communities (Kiryas Joel, independent schools) preferring autonomy over central authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; Jewish tradition mixes repentance and punishment, and the sources give no political stance.

traditional-family.rationale: Teitelbaum insisted on strict family purity laws, modesty and traditional marital customs, so strong agreement is a documented part of the community's practice.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Satmar practice is strict halakhic orthodoxy, which treats same-sex marriage as prohibited; the sources show strong conservatism.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from strictly orthodox Jewish law, which permits abortion only in narrow cases such as danger to the mother.

more-religion-public.rationale: Haredim wish religion to shape communal life, but anti-Zionists reject a state-run religious public sphere under Zionist government, so agreement is moderate.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents have no stated position.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The community enforces distinct, religiously fixed roles for men and women, so the claim that gender is mainly constructed is rejected.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Zionist nationalism and a revived Hebrew culture are rejected; Jewish identity is defined by Torah and exile, not national culture. Preserving religious tradition is strongly held but that is not national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred from strong traditionalism and Teitelbaum's rejection of modernity and the Haskalah.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; the community lives as a minority in diaspora countries and has no stated immigration-level position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: Haredi anti-Zionists do appeal to the UN (Dushinsky told it he opposed a Jewish state), but there is no sign they want it strengthened.

free-trade.rationale: Haredi communities are commercially active but the sources give no view on trade policy, and the community's concern is religious autonomy rather than market doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred: Jewish national self-assertion is rejected; Jews are to live peaceably in their host nations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that Jews should not wage war or rebel against nations; no direct treatment.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; the sources never take a stance on borders in general.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: large families are valued in Haredi life, so growth-limiting ideas are unlikely to be endorsed, though no source addresses it directly.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Neither Satmar texts nor surveys of Haredi politics take up climate policy; Haredi voters have mostly prioritised religious and funding issues, so no lean is inferable.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Teitelbaum rejected modernity and banned television; salvation comes through the Messiah, not technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy does not appear in any source; with no theological or communal stake, adherents have no stated view.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Three Oaths forbid rebelling against the nations; the primary text presents rebellion as a violation with grave consequences, so adherents are strongly opposed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; authority rests with rabbinic scholars rather than secular experts or the public.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from the community's practice of running independent institutions and refusing state money, which favours autonomy over state direction of the economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ownership structure of firms is not discussed; Haredi enclaves host family businesses and some cooperatives, so adherents are indifferent.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is not addressed in any source and has no religious valence, so adherents would have no particular answer.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from halakhic inheritance law and family-oriented values; no direct source.

basic-income.rationale: A state payment is something Satmar avoids in Israel, but in the diaspora Haredim accept benefits; the sources do not decide the question.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection has no connection to the Three Oaths or Satmar practice, and no source takes a position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred: the community refuses state funds and the Zionist state's initiatives, so state direction of investment is unwelcome.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: Haredi enclaves are built on family homes and small businesses, which fits dispersed ownership more than state or corporate concentration.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred: a traditional community with commerce and wage work has no program to abolish money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in any source consulted, so no position can be attributed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: state-recognised bodies setting wages are state structures that Satmar avoids.

one-party-rule.rationale: Satmar forbids even voting and membership in the Israeli state; a party guiding a state by its ideology is the opposite of a Torah-led, state-avoiding stance.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; tradition values a future Davidic king but no source states a view on present monarchies.

democracy-best.rationale: Anti-Zionists tell followers not to participate in elections and see voting as partnership in sin, though the primary sources do not argue about democracy as such.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from the prohibition on voting in Israeli elections and a rabbi-led authority structure.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: secular council power is alien to a rabbinically governed community.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; adherents deny the Israeli state's legitimacy but have not stated a general secession principle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; rabbinic and Rebbe authority is accepted, but no source states this as natural rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Three Oaths bar Jews from forcing redemption or rebelling against the nations; the Satmar position holds that violence to establish a state is forbidden.

war-builds-character.rationale: War to establish Jewish sovereignty is a violation of the oaths; Satmar sees Israeli wars as divine punishment rather than ennobling.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents want halakha to govern Jewish life but reject a Jewish state before the Messiah, so they are split in effect.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Torah law governs Jewish life, but they deny that a Zionist state may legitimately enforce it, so agreement is reduced.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: the community runs its own rabbinic courts for civil matters, but defence by private companies is not discussed.

military-superiority.rationale: Satmar views Israeli military power as part of the forbidden rebellion; armed superiority is not a goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Jewish identity is religious (covenant of Torah), and ethnic nationalism is rejected as the heresy of Zionism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Secular materialist historiography is rejected, history being guided by divine providence.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: tradition values charity but not state-engineered equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed directly; NK supports Palestinian control of the land but that is not framed in indigenous terms.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources do not take up reparations; the Haredi anti-Zionist case concerns Zionism, not European colonialism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: Haredi anti-Zionists are a diaspora minority who disavow political unity projects, though NK has aligned with Iran.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred from Torah ethics emphasising duty and charity.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from halakhic obligation as the basis of communal life.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Jewish tradition values creation as God's work yet Teitelbaum's writings in the sources say nothing on nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: large families are valued in Hasidic life.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Teitelbaum rejected modernity but there is no anti-industrial program.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Teitelbaum rejected modernity and banned television, so speeding up disruptive technology is opposed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from Teitelbaum's rejection of modernity and his bans on television, which indicate hostility to technological alteration of human life.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: rabbinic authority governs the community, and nothing suggests handing decisions to AI.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not a theme of the Haredi anti-Zionist sources, so no lean is inferable.

restore-past-order.rationale: Teitelbaum resisted modernity and insisted on traditional customs, valuing continuity over progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: halakhic principle, not results, governs, as in Teitelbaum's insistence on the oaths whatever the outcome.

direct-action.rationale: Zionism itself is condemned as impatient forcing of the end; adherents avoid elections, but direct action in the usual political sense is not endorsed.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from Vayoel Moshe's insistence that redemption cannot be reached by forcing it through human means; the manner of action must fit the divine order.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the tradition supports it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred: a traditional community with distinct gender and scholar roles would reject abolishing specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Charity (tzedakah) responds to need, but a general rule of distribution by need over work is not a stated Haredi teaching.

production-for-use.rationale: Not a theme in any source; Hasidic communities run commercial businesses but have no stated view on the profit principle.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: Marxist exploitation theory is a secular materialist doctrine foreign to Haredi thought.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Secular revolution is opposed under the oath against rebellion and by religious principle.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred: Haredi anti-Zionists do not follow the collectivist agricultural ideals of the kibbutz, which belonged to secular Zionism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: wars in the Middle East are attributed to violation of the oaths, not economics.

taxation-theft.rationale: Teitelbaum urged peaceful citizenship under gentile governments; taxation as theft is not a stated view.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred: religious law restricts conduct beyond harm to others, as with strict modesty rules.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred: communal Torah life is prior to individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Most Haredi groups refuse IDF service and protest conscription of yeshiva students.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; adherents refuse to vote but the claim about freedom to leave being a stronger check is not made.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: treating the state as a provider and citizens as customers is foreign to a community that avoids relying on the state at all.

positive-liberty.rationale: The sources do not discuss freedom as material capacity; the Satmar emphasis is on religious duty rather than liberty theory.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred from Teitelbaum's ban on television and distrust of secular culture, which implies seeing media and universities as powerful forces against the faithful.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred: Jewish thought sees descent but not racial genetic ranking; no source.

organic-representation.rationale: The Satmar community is organised through the Rebbe, family and community bodies, which fits organic representation, but adherents refuse electoral politics so the question hardly arises.

total-state.rationale: The community builds autonomous institutions and avoids the state; a total state is the opposite.

national-rebirth.rationale: Zionism's national rebirth is condemned as heresy.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Settlement and force to take the Land violates the oaths.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Hasidic loyalty to the Rebbe is personal but it is not feudal lord-follower rule.

bound-labor.rationale: Inferred: not part of the tradition.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: Torah is held to be objective divine truth and not a product of social power, so the claim that all knowledge reflects power is rejected.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred from Torah as universal truth.

single-common-good.rationale: Torah supplies a single divine standard, but the sources do not frame politics as seeking a common good, so adherents split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Vayoel Moshe states that a Jewish state before the Messiah is a forbidden rebellion that postpones redemption; this is the core position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Mass return to the Land before redemption is forbidden by the oaths, though individual residence is allowed.

revive-national-language.rationale: Vayoel Moshe argues that speaking modern Hebrew as a vernacular is forbidden.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred: Haredi communities generally structure authority hierarchically, as in the Rebbe's court, and have no programme of worker voting rights.

school-vouchers.rationale: Haredim run independent schools and favour public funding for them; Satmar's own Israeli schools are funded from abroad, so the lean is modest.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is outside what the sources discuss.

economic-freedom.rationale: No source treats the link between economic and political freedom, and adherents do not claim political freedom as their goal.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from the Rebbe model, where moral and religious authority leads by personal example rather than state coercion.

national-self-determination.rationale: Jewish national self-determination is rejected; for other nations, no stated view, so the answer is mild.

force-without-un.rationale: Force by Jews to take land violates the oaths; adherents appeal to the UN rather than bypass it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Teitelbaum's work is grounded in Talmudic authority and faith; the claim that reason alone should guide is rejected.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not discussed; Haredi communities often include immigrants themselves, so there is no clear lean.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; Haredi Torah study conflicts with work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: Inferred: traditional religious society values harmony.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Teitelbaum preserved inherited customs against modernity, so sacrificing inherited institutions for new creation is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: NK's alignments with Iran exist but are fringe; mainstream Satmar rejects.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred: organising a class along national lines is a nationalist project of the kind Haredi anti-Zionists oppose.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Teitelbaum enforced distinct roles, but law-in-public-life is a statement about state law, which they would rather not apply.

ban-interest.rationale: The Torah prohibits interest between Jews but a state ban is not discussed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred from the Jewish minority condition and equal moral worth; the oaths call for peaceful coexistence with host nations, not state racial classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist theory of the state not discussed in any Haredi source; adherents see the Zionist state as illegitimate on religious, not class, grounds.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production has no religious or Zionism-related stake in the sources, so adherents do not take a side.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Teitelbaum insisted Hasidim look distinct to resist assimilation, so assimilation as a norm is rejected.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: a conspiracy theory not part of the doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems matter to Haredi parties, but Satmar forbids voting at all, so the electoral design question does not arise for adherents.

national-mission.rationale: A national mission to spread a government is foreign to the doctrine.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Strict gender roles are seen as divinely ordained.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inferred from the Satmar view that the Zionist leadership is heretical and that participating in its politics is sinful.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: Haredi communities, with strong pronatalism and halakhic teaching, oppose state discouragement of births.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from NK's critique of Israeli conduct toward Palestinians.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A minimal state is not discussed; Satmar wants nothing from the Israeli state but defends its own communal institutions in the diaspora.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred: Halakha restricts intermarriage by religion, not race, so a racial rule is not a Jewish teaching, though the community does discourage marrying outside the faith.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred: Jews should live peacefully among nations.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate outside the Haredi sources.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: NK supports transferring control to Palestinians, reflecting a view of the Zionist state as illegitimate.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Haredim seek own rabbinic courts and community autonomy.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Judaism discourages conversion and does not proselytise, but adherents are split over whether the law should restrict it, and no source addresses the matter.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Kosher ritual slaughter of cattle is required by halakha, so a ban would harm Haredi practice.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Haredim run independent religious schools and mostly do not want a ban.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: a state surrounded by enemies strengthening itself is the logic of the Zionist state the doctrine opposes.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The sources never address legitimacy theory; Satmar locates authority in Torah, not consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade policy is not addressed by any source.

population-transfer.rationale: NK supports return of the land to the Palestinians, and the Vayoel Moshe line opposes forced population movement as part of the Zionist project.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Inferred from the Three Oaths, which bar forcing the end and rebelling, but the doctrine allows communal self-defence, so only mild agreement.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred: progress is defined by Torah and redemption, so social Darwinist struggle is rejected.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not discussed; Haredi anti-Zionists face this issue as outsiders to party politics.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican theory of freedom is not in any source.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not treated; Satmar rejects participation in Israeli institutions altogether.

vanguard-party.rationale: A party leading revolution is a form of the rebellion barred by the oaths and a secular route to salvation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred: charity to the poor is central to halakhic life, although no source frames it as a duty of law and institutions.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A UK housing policy not addressed by any source.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not discussed, and Haredi communities have no stated stance.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: large families are a blessing in Haredi thought, so blaming population for poverty is rejected.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Haredi enclaves prize homogeneity but the sources never argue about diversity and cohesion for society at large.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: leadership in Satmar passes within a rabbinic dynasty, so filling offices by lottery has no place.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the community's status as a minority needing protections and a doctrine of peaceful co-citizenship.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No source speaks to price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: a community that avoids television and distrusts state institutions would not support state control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that Jews should not take up arms for a state before redemption.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are not covered; the Satmar view concerns Jewish immigration to Israel, which it opposes en masse.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed, and Satmar adherents do not stand for office.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parties are not an organising form for Satmar, which sits outside party politics.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational integration is not addressed by the sources.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of military power as a political tool and the doctrine of submission to gentile governments.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The question concerns a church hierarchy and has no counterpart in Judaism, so adherents have no answer.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rebbes and rabbinic courts hold ultimate authority in the community.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from the oath against rebelling against the nations, which argues for loyalty rather than for working for a government's defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Teitelbaum prohibited television and enforced modesty norms.

recall-officials.rationale: Not discussed; adherents do not take part in elections to Israeli bodies, so recall is not an issue for them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Satmar opposes Israeli military action, yet the question of alliances is not addressed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: renting is normal in Haredi communities and halakha regulates it.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine against Jews taking up arms to establish a state and the refusal of military service.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Hasidic communities are urban or suburban, and the sources make no claim about rural virtue.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred: reuniting a nation is a nationalist aim, and the doctrine is wary of national projects.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from Teitelbaum's rejection of the Haskalah and secular learning, which implies distrust of university-educated elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Judaism sees a chosen covenant, but Satmar sources do not rank civilisations.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: the Torah prescribes capital punishment for grave crimes, so conservative adherents do not object in principle to executing terrorists, though rabbinic tradition hedges it heavily.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Teitelbaum enforced strict modesty norms, so school sex and gender-equality curricula are opposed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: Haredi schools teach Torah creation, so adherents favour teaching it alongside evolution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Teitelbaum's strict modesty rules and prohibition of television imply strong support for restricting pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: Jewish identity passes by descent from the mother, and a community built on lineage and tradition tends to accept descent-based membership, though no source discusses state citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from Yiddish and Hebrew language preferences.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Haredim seek exemption from military service and other laws burdening observance.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from Teitelbaum's insistence on uniform dress and customs, which values conformity to Torah over eccentric lives.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-writing is not addressed, and adherents reject participation in Israeli statecraft.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: development is not a Haredi aim, and rejecting political freedoms for growth does not fit a minority wanting freedom of religion.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the duty of tzedakah, though no source extends it to global aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: Satmar's rejection of Israeli military strength implies opposition to nuclear arms.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: No source addresses how a head of state should be chosen; adherents hold no doctrine on it.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside anything the Satmar or Haredi sources discuss.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The land is not a political asset to be held by force before the Messiah, so anti-Zionists would not refuse concessions on principle; NK even backs Palestinian rule over all of it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Halakha both protects property and demands charity, but sources give no political formulation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that the Haredi sources never enter.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental policy is not addressed in any source used.

collective-defense.rationale: The oaths rule out Jewish war-making; allied collective defence for other states is not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: NK and Satmar reject Israeli rule in the territories as illegitimate; Teitelbaum forbade prayer at occupied sites to avoid legitimising it.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Rabbinic authority and independent communal institutions are central; placing clergy under civil authority is opposed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine against war-making and for peaceful life under governments.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No stated view; the community prizes autonomy but there is no source on regional federalism.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Only the Messiah, not a human head of state, holds sacred kingship; divine-descent claims for rulers are foreign to Judaism.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not discussed in the sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: The sources do not discuss this nature-nurture question.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from Jewish law's view that even the king is bound by Torah.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from Teitelbaum's rejection of modernity and focus on Torah life.

leader-cult.rationale: A national leader embodying the nation is idolatry-adjacent for Haredim; Rebbe veneration is religious, not national.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is outside any source consulted.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate that does not concern Haredi anti-Zionists.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; the sources are silent on agrarian policy.

refugee-return.rationale: NK calls for return of land to Palestinians and a state where they control the whole territory, implying refugee return; Satmar mainstream is less explicit.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claiming land on grounds of nationality is the Zionist premise they reject.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: without a Jewish state before the Messiah, Satmar teaches no legal punishment, and the community enforces norms through social sanction and herem instead.

women-must-cover.rationale: Satmar mandates modesty norms for its own women (stockings, hair covering), but the statement asks about state law, which Satmar would not enforce, so no clear lean.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: National unification of a people across borders is the nationalist logic they reject.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Satmar model is self-governing community institutions and schools within the host state, not a state of its own.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The doctrine holds that Jews should live as peaceful citizens of other nations rather than found a state; Vayoel Moshe frames this as a religious duty, though without advocating a campaign for rights.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical change is guided by divine providence, not economic production.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: No source speaks to constitutional constraints on majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Strict separation of gender roles under Teitelbaum's rule makes quotas for parity foreign.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed at state level, although Satmar communities seek their own institutional self-sufficiency.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Haredi life centres on religious duty over material reward, as in Torah study that is unpaid.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rebelling against the nations is forbidden by the oaths; the primary text treats armed forcing of events as heresy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hasidic dynasties pass leadership by descent, so abolishing hereditary privilege is not a goal.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: Jewish rule over others is not a project of the doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: National flag, anthem and pride in the Israeli state are rejected, and Satmar schools in Israel remain independent of state.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: cultivating influence over former imperial space is a nationalist power project, not part of the doctrine.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek exemptions for religious practice but no sources state a general principle.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: a religious minority relying on guaranteed freedoms of religion in diaspora states benefits from entrenched rights, though no source states it.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; Haredi minority parties seek vetoes on religious matters, but Satmar does not take part in such bargaining.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The oaths forbid rebellion against the nations, so resistance by removal is rejected even if rulers are oppressive.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Jewish law forbids cruelty to animals (tza'ar ba'alei chayim).

animal-use-humane.rationale: Kosher slaughter and animal use are accepted under halakha.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Tzedakah is an obligation of the wealthy in halakha, but the sources do not frame it as noblesse oblige.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Satmar bans voting, membership of state institutions and acceptance of its money, urging withdrawal from the Zionist political order.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the television ban, though the critical-theory claim itself is not stated in sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not discussed; Satmar sources do not use class-hegemony analysis.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Satmar refuses state welfare and funds its Israeli schools from abroad, preferring independence from the state.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Reclaiming land by force is a violation of the oaths.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: NK supports Palestinian political control, but not in indigenous terms.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not discussed; Haredi anti-Zionists have no stake in national monuments and no source reports a view.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military power as a political guardian is contrary to the oath against rebelling.

filial-duty.rationale: Honouring parents is a Torah commandment central to Hasidic life.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Halakhic divorce requires a get granted by the husband, not unilateral exit, but this is not stated for the state.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: halakha recognises private ownership of land, so community tenure by use is not a Haredi position.

single-official-language.rationale: Teitelbaum's ban on Modern Hebrew as a spoken vernacular shows rejection of a state imposing one national language; Yiddish is the community language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; the Satmar view is that Jews should not mass-settle the Land, not about foreign ownership.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from Teitelbaum's ascetic and modest rules, such as bans on television, which treat acquisitive culture as harmful.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the oath against rebellion and doctrine against violence for political ends.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine that Jews should not wage war and should live peacefully under their nations.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not discussed in any source consulted, so no position can be attributed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Satmar schools in Israel are funded from abroad, so restricting foreign funding would harm them.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: Haredi life prizes large families, so state incentives for births fit their values, though the sources do not discuss it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from enclave communities like Kiryas Joel.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed in any source consulted, so no position can be attributed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Teitelbaum urged peaceful citizenship under gentile governments, implying a duty to obey.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy theory against a minority is contrary to their own situation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is a religious institution with halakhic rules, so removing its legal status is opposed.

local-production.rationale: Not discussed; Haredi communities buy within their own enclaves but sources give no economic doctrine.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed; Satmar appeals to international bodies like the UN against the state but gives no general rule.

religious-nation.rationale: Jewishness is a religious community, but defining a nation by religion as a political project is Zionist-adjacent.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: Satmar communities prefer self-funded independent institutions, which fits local control of money, but no source states a regional-revenue view.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: Halakha protects private property, so personal belongings remaining private is natural.

religion-illusion.rationale: Teitelbaum's whole worldview is religious faith.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Teitelbaum enforced distinct religious roles for women, so equality via economic transformation is rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: Family and mother-led child-rearing are central to Hasidic life, so public provision replacing it is opposed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is a nationalist project; Hebrew vernacular is forbidden.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Satmar enclaves are self-governing communities, though private property is retained.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine against settlement and mass return before redemption.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Vayoel Moshe holds that the Land's religious tie gives no right to take it before redemption; individual residence is only optional.

holocaust-denial.rationale: NK's spokesman called the Holocaust irrefutable, and Satmar rebbe lived through it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Halakha prohibits male same-sex relations, but Satmar sources ask no state to criminalise it and the community lives under liberal diaspora law, so only a mild lean against criminalisation is inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred from Satmar's minority position, though rabbinic courts use herem against dissidents.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: Halakha treats blasphemy as a grave offence and traditional communities support punishing it, though Satmar would not ask the Zionist state to do so.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine against Jews dominating others and the NK critique of Zionist dispossession.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Jewish doctrine here bars rebellion and armed resistance by Jews; Muslim duties are not taken up, but NK still rejects violence.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Rebelling against rulers, even secular ones, is forbidden.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the refusal to take part in elections and a rabbinic authority structure.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Strict gender roles under Teitelbaum mean that legal recognition of gender identity is rejected.

assisted-dying.rationale: Halakha prohibits hastening death, so assisted dying is opposed by orthodox rabbinic authorities.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not discussed; Satmar refuses party politics entirely and places itself outside the left-right division, but sources do not state it as a claim.

islam-incompatible.rationale: NK supports Palestinians and works with Muslims; they reject the claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Vayoel Moshe founds Jewish political life on divine command and redemption through God alone, and denies human sovereign action before the Messiah.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Distinctive dress is mandated by Teitelbaum to resist assimilation, so bans on religious dress in state settings are opposed.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The doctrine opposes Jewish war-making but sources do not address other states.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of not rebelling or warring and of living peaceably among nations.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Satmar rebbes pass leadership within the family.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from Jewish interest prohibitions and gemach free-loan funds, which are common in Haredi communities.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: Satmar refuses voting entirely, and restricting franchise to owners has no basis in its teaching.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Foreign to the Torah-centred worldview; Satmar teaching assigns women distinct religious roles.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from halakha as fixed law applied by known rabbinic judges.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred from equal moral worth and a minority interest in equal civil rights.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from the community's restrictions on internet and television use.

open-government-data.rationale: Not discussed in any source consulted, so no position can be attributed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Halakha forbids intermarriage and the community enforces it socially, though the legal restriction question is not addressed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of peaceful co-existence with other nations.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: authority in the community lies with rabbis and the Rebbe, not randomly chosen laypeople, though no source discusses assemblies.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from strict orthodoxy and refusal of military service itself.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Teitelbaum's worldview is built on religious faith and Torah education, so state atheism is strongly rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: halakha requires courts and punishment, so abolition is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not discussed in any source consulted, so no position can be attributed.

missingStatements.text: Jews should not establish a sovereign state before the coming of the Messiah.
missingStatements.rationale: The Three Oaths argument of Vayoel Moshe is the defining claim, and no existing statement captures its messianic timing.

missingStatements.text: Citizens of a religious minority should refuse to vote in or take funds from a state they hold to be illegitimate.
missingStatements.rationale: Satmar bans voting and acceptance of state welfare as a principle of non-recognition.
missingStatements.declined: Niche Satmar practice; too specific to one community to be asked of every ideology.

missingStatements.text: The everyday spoken language of a religious community should remain separate from its sacred language.
missingStatements.rationale: Vayoel Moshe forbids Modern Hebrew as a vernacular, reserving Hebrew for prayer and study.

notes: Neturei Karta goes beyond Satmar by seeking the state's dismantling and allying with Iran; Satmar disavows it. Agudat Yisrael and Litvish Haredim take part in elections and accept funds.
